evals.query: I have a Kora 2.0 Java service. Consume plain String messages from the topic configured at kafka.consumer.userEvents and log each value.
expected_behavior: Annotates a method on a @Component class with @KafkaListener("kafka.consumer.userEvents") imported from io.koraframework.kafka.common.annotation
Imports @Component from io.koraframework.common.annotation
Uses the void process(String value) signature and does not declare a Consumer parameter
Adds io.koraframework:kafka through the io.koraframework:kora-bom platform, plus annotationProcessor "io.koraframework:annotation-processors"
Adds KafkaModule to the @KoraApp interface with extends, and does not add the generated <Class>Module to that extends clause
Creates application.conf with kafka.consumer.userEvents.topics and driverProperties bootstrap.servers
Does not use the ru.tinkoff.kora group, the kora-parent BOM or any ru.tinkoff.kora.* import
Uses constructor injection for any collaborator; no field injection

evals.query: Set up a Kafka listener in my Kora 2.0 Kotlin service that reads String values from kafka.consumer.userEvents.
expected_behavior: Applies the com.google.devtools.ksp plugin and adds ksp("io.koraframework:symbol-processors") — not annotationProcessor and not kapt
Adds implementation("io.koraframework:kafka") with the io.koraframework:kora-bom platform
Declares a plain `fun process(value: String)` annotated @KafkaListener on a @Component class
Does not declare the listener as `suspend fun`, does not return a reactive type, and does not wrap the body in runBlocking or withContext(Dispatchers.IO)
Adds KafkaModule to the @KoraApp interface
Does not use ru.tinkoff.kora.* imports

evals.query: Port this Kora 1.x Kotlin listener to Kora 2.0: `@KafkaListener("kafka.consumer.orders") suspend fun process(record: ConsumerRecord<String, String>) = withContext(Dispatchers.IO) { repo.save(record.value()) }`
expected_behavior: Removes `suspend` and produces a plain `fun process(record: ConsumerRecord<String, String>)`
Removes withContext(Dispatchers.IO) / runBlocking entirely rather than replacing it with another coroutine construct

Explains that the single-ConsumerRecord shape has no suspend handling in KSP at all, so this exact listener generates Kotlin that does not compile; and that listeners run on the poll thread, so dispatching to another pool adds overhead without benefit
Keeps the repository call as a direct synchronous call
Does not introduce kotlinx-coroutines as a dependency to make the listener compile

Does not suggest Mono, Flux or CompletionStage as a listener return type, and if it mentions them, says they are silently ignored rather than rejected — the container never awaits the result and commits the offset as soon as the method returns

evals.query: My Kora 1.x listener took a Context parameter to read an MDC value: `void process(String value, Context context)`. How do I do that in Kora 2.0?
expected_behavior: States that Context has been removed from Kora 2.0 entirely — there is no io.koraframework Context type to import
Removes the Context parameter rather than renaming or re-importing it
Explains that an unrecognised parameter makes the processor fail with "Kafka record listener method has unsupported parameter", or is misread as a payload parameter
Points at io.koraframework.logging.common.MDC, which the record handler already scopes around each record, for MDC access
Does not invent a Kora 2.0 Context, RequestContext or telemetry-context parameter

evals.query: Port this listener to Kora 2.0: `void process(ConsumerRecord<String, String> record, KafkaConsumerTelemetry.KafkaConsumerRecordTelemetryContext<String, String> ctx)`.
expected_behavior: States that KafkaConsumerTelemetry has no nested KafkaConsumerRecordTelemetryContext / KafkaConsumerRecordsTelemetryContext type in Kora 2.0
Removes the telemetry parameter, leaving an accepted signature
Notes that the 2.0 observation types are KafkaConsumerPollObservation and KafkaConsumerRecordObservation and that neither is injectable as a listener parameter
Points at telemetry configuration (telemetry.logging / telemetry.metrics / telemetry.tracing) or a DefaultKafkaConsumerLoggerFactory subclass for custom instrumentation
Does not keep the parameter with an adjusted import

evals.query: This listener will not compile: `@KafkaListener("kafka.consumer.orders") void process(OrderService service, String key, String value, Headers headers)`. The error is "Kafka listener method has too many payload parameters". Fix it.
expected_behavior: Removes OrderService from the parameter list and injects it through the listener class constructor instead
Keeps a signature the processor accepts, such as process(String key, String value, Headers headers)
Explains that the processor classifies parameters by type and treats anything it does not recognise as a payload, allowing at most two payload parameters (key then value)
Does not add an annotation to the service parameter to make it injectable
Does not suggest field injection or a static holder

evals.query: My batch listener `void process(ConsumerRecords<String, String> records, Headers headers, Exception exception)` fails with "Kafka records listener method has unsupported parameter". Why?
expected_behavior: Explains that a batch (ConsumerRecords) listener accepts only ConsumerRecords and Consumer parameters
Removes the Headers and Exception parameters
Shows reading headers per record inside the loop with record.headers()
Shows catching RecordValueDeserializationException around record.value() inside the loop, because a batch listener has no exception parameter
Notes that KafkaSkipRecordException has no effect in a batch listener — the batch handler has no skip branch — so filtering must be explicit

evals.query: In my Kora 2.0 Kotlin service I want a listener that receives the key, the value, the record headers and any deserialization error: `@KafkaListener("kafka.consumer.orders") fun process(key: String?, value: String?, headers: Headers, exception: Exception?)`. Is this signature supported?
expected_behavior: Confirms the signature is supported by KSP as it is by the Java processor (covered by KafkaListenerKeyAndValueTest#testProcessKeyValueHeaderAndException)
Keeps key and value nullable because the generated code passes null when deserialization fails, and takes org.apache.kafka.common.header.Headers
Writes a plain `fun`, not `suspend fun`
Does not describe a KSP compile defect for Headers plus an exception parameter, and does not tell the user to switch to ConsumerRecord as a workaround

evals.query: Deserialize incoming Kafka messages into a UserEvent record with userId and eventType fields using Kora 2.0 JSON.
expected_behavior: Annotates the record with @Json from io.koraframework.json.common.annotation
Annotates the listener parameter with @Json, e.g. void process(@Json UserEvent event)
Adds the io.koraframework:json-common dependency and JsonModule from io.koraframework.json.common to the @KoraApp interface
Does not reference the ru.tinkoff.kora:json-module artifact or ru.tinkoff.kora.json.module.JsonModule
Does not set key.deserializer / value.deserializer in driverProperties for the JSON value

evals.query: Write a custom Kafka Deserializer in Kotlin for my Kora 2.0 service that turns bytes into an OrderEvent using the generated JsonReader.
expected_behavior: Implements org.apache.kafka.common.serialization.Deserializer<OrderEvent>, annotated @Component and @Tag(OrderEvent::class)
Wraps the read in requireNotNull, e.g. `requireNotNull(reader.read(data))`, because JsonReader<T>.read returns a nullable T
Does not assign reader.read(data) straight to a non-null return type

Declares `override fun deserialize(topic: String, data: ByteArray): OrderEvent` matching the @NullMarked contract, and mentions that a mismatch reports "'deserialize' overrides nothing" without naming nullability
References the same @Tag on the listener parameter so the deserializer is actually selected
Does not wrap the call in try/catch (IOException) — JsonReader.read declares only the unchecked tools.jackson.core.JacksonException

evals.query: Make my JSON Kafka listener resilient: when a message fails to deserialize, log it and continue instead of restarting the consumer.
expected_behavior: Uses the nullable signature void process(@Nullable @Json Event event, @Nullable Exception exception)
Imports @Nullable from org.jspecify.annotations, not from jakarta.annotation or javax.annotation
In Kotlin writes the nullability into the types (`event: Event?, exception: Exception?`) instead of using an annotation
Checks exception != null before touching the event, and also handles event == null
Explains that an uncaught exception ends the poll loop, waits backoffTimeout and rebuilds the consumer, so the record is redelivered
Optionally mentions RecordValueDeserializationException.getRecord() returning the raw ConsumerRecord<byte[], byte[]> for a DLQ

evals.query: Skip messages whose userId is blank in my Kora 2.0 Kafka listener, while still reporting them to telemetry.
expected_behavior: Throws KafkaSkipRecordException imported from io.koraframework.kafka.common.exceptions
Passes a cause to the constructor, which takes a non-null Throwable and has no message-only form
States that the record is reported as an error to telemetry, the offset is committed and the loop continues to the next record
Mentions SkippableRecordException as the marker interface for a family of business exceptions
Notes that this only works in a single-record listener, not in a ConsumerRecords batch listener
Does not throw a plain RuntimeException expecting the container to skip it

evals.query: I need the Kafka offset committed only after the database write succeeds in my Kora 2.0 service. Right now my config has "enable.auto.commit" = true.
expected_behavior: Adds a Consumer<K, V> parameter to the @KafkaListener method and calls consumer.commitSync() after the write
Removes "enable.auto.commit" = true, explaining that it hands committing to the driver's timer, which can commit ahead of the handler
Explains that declaring a Consumer parameter switches Kora's automatic commit off for that listener, so forgetting commitSync() means the group never advances
Mentions that with no Consumer parameter and enable.auto.commit unset, Kora already commits offset+1 after each record returns
Does not commit before the business logic and does not commit inside a catch block that swallows the failure

evals.query: In my Kora 2.0 service I want every instance to receive every message from the topics `prices` and `rates`. How do I configure the listener?
expected_behavior: Identifies the assign strategy (no group.id in driverProperties) as the broadcast mechanism
Uses one kafka.consumer section with topics = ["prices", "rates"]; the assign container reads every partition of every listed topic

States that topicsPattern is rejected in assign mode: KafkaAssignConsumerContainer fails fast with "does not support topicsPattern, please specify topics instead", and an empty topics list fails with "requires at least one topic"
Mentions that the assign container never commits offsets, so `offset` (earliest / latest / a Duration) decides where each start begins
Does not claim assign mode accepts only a single topic and does not split the topics into two sections for that reason

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 Kafka consumer publishes no messaging metrics and writes no log lines at all, not even a startup message. The config has a telemetry block. What is wrong?
expected_behavior: States that telemetry.logging.enabled and telemetry.metrics.enabled both default to false in Kora 2.0, while telemetry.tracing.enabled defaults to true
Enables them explicitly under the listener's own kafka.consumer.<name>.telemetry block
Explains that telemetry.logging.enabled also gates the container's own lifecycle logging, which is why the consumer is completely silent
Notes that a MeterRegistry (micrometer-module) and a Tracer (opentelemetry-tracing) must be in the graph or the enabled flags still produce nothing
Names the real meters — messaging.process.duration, messaging.process.batch.duration and messaging.kafka.consumer.lag — and notes that the lag gauge is reported only in assign mode
Does not claim telemetry is enabled by default

evals.query: In Kora 1.x I registered a custom KafkaConsumerLoggerFactory component to change how consumed records are logged. Port it to Kora 2.0.
expected_behavior: States that no KafkaConsumerLoggerFactory interface exists in Kora 2.0

Registers a @Component that extends the concrete class io.koraframework.kafka.common.consumer.telemetry.impl.DefaultKafkaConsumerLoggerFactory and overrides create(DefaultKafkaConsumerTelemetry.TelemetryContext)

Calls super(maskingStrategy, bodyConverter) with the injected @Tag(KafkaConsumerTelemetry.class) MaskingStrategy and DefaultKafkaConsumerBodyConverter, and builds DefaultKafkaConsumerLogger with (logger, maskingStrategy, bodyConverter, context) — there is no no-arg or (logger, context) constructor

Explains that KafkaListenerModule (pulled in by KafkaModule) declares defaultKafkaConsumerTelemetryFactory as a @DefaultComponent whose @Nullable DefaultKafkaConsumerLoggerFactory parameter picks the component up
Notes that the custom factory is consulted only when telemetry.logging.enabled = true, otherwise NoopKafkaConsumerLoggerFactory is substituted

Mentions the broader options — subclassing DefaultKafkaConsumerTelemetryFactory, or supplying a KafkaConsumerTelemetryFactory @Component that replaces the default for every listener — and that configuration (tags, attributes, slo, driverMetrics) covers many cases
Does not claim custom telemetry listeners are impossible in 2.0, and does not keep the 1.x interface with a renamed import

evals.query: Commit offsets and clear a local cache when partitions are revoked during a Kafka rebalance in my Kora 2.0 service.
expected_behavior: Implements io.koraframework.kafka.common.consumer.ConsumerAwareRebalanceListener as a @Component
Annotates it with @Tag from io.koraframework.common.annotation matching the listener — either the generated <Class>Module.<Class><Method>Tag or an explicit class passed to @KafkaListener(tag = ...)
Commits in onPartitionsRevoked with consumer.commitSync() and explicitly overrides onPartitionsLost so it does not commit
Notes that the default onPartitionsLost delegates to onPartitionsRevoked, so a committing revoke path must be overridden
Warns that the rebalance listener parameter is @Nullable, so a tag mismatch fails silently with no warning
Notes that rebalance callbacks only exist in subscribe mode, not with the assign strategy
Does not use the raw org.apache.kafka ConsumerRebalanceListener or a Spring-style @Qualifier

evals.query: Write an integration test for my Kora 2.0 Kafka listener that spins up a real broker with Testcontainers.
expected_behavior: Uses @KoraAppTest(Application.class) with KoraAppTestConfigModifier and injects the listener with @TestComponent

Injects the generated container as a tagged Lifecycle — @Tag(<Class>Module.<Class><Method>Tag.class) @TestComponent Lifecycle — and explains that without it @KoraAppTest prunes the container and the listener never starts
Overrides bootstrap.servers via KoraConfigModification.ofSystemProperty (or ofString/withSystemProperty) rather than editing application.conf

Uses the Testcontainers 2.x coordinates: org.testcontainers:testcontainers-kafka with org.testcontainers.kafka.KafkaContainer, or the io.goodforgod:testcontainers-extensions-kafka extension the Kora 2.0 examples use
Does not reference org.testcontainers:kafka or org.testcontainers.containers.KafkaContainer
Sets auto.offset.reset = "earliest" so records produced before the consumer joins are still delivered
Asserts asynchronously with Awaitility against state the listener records, rather than asserting immediately after send
Does not mock the @KafkaListener method

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 Kafka config has `"bootstrap.servers" = ${KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP:"localhost:9092"}` and the app will not start. Fix the config.
expected_behavior: States that HOCON has no ${VAR:default} placeholder — that form is not valid HOCON
Replaces it with the literal-then-override pattern: assign "localhost:9092" first, then reassign with ${?KAFKA_BOOTSTRAP} on the next line
Explains that ${VAR} is a required substitution that aborts startup when unset, while ${?VAR} is optional
Keeps the later assignment after the literal, since the last assignment wins
Does not read the variable with System.getenv in code as the fix

evals.query: After consuming a record in my Kora 2.0 service I want to publish a derived message and commit the consumer offset atomically with it.
expected_behavior:
Declares a @KafkaPublisher interface extending TransactionalPublisher

from io.koraframework.kafka.common.producer, wrapping a nested @KafkaPublisher interface with the @Topic methods
Declares a Consumer<K, V> parameter on the listener, both for consumer.groupMetadata() and to stop Kora committing outside the transaction
Uses withTx(transaction -> ...) (or begin().use { } in Kotlin) and calls transaction.sendOffsetsToTransaction(offsets, consumer.groupMetadata()) with offset + 1
Sets "isolation.level" = "read_committed" on the downstream consumer
Configures idPrefix / maxPoolSize / maxWaitTime on the transactional publisher's own config section
Notes that Kotlin cannot resolve the inTx/withTx overloads from a bare lambda, so begin().use { } or an explicit SAM constructor is required
Does not invent a @KoraTransaction annotation or a transaction listener parameter

evals.query: My Kora 2.0 listener has `topicsPattern = "prices-.*"` and no group.id in driverProperties, because every instance should read everything. The application fails to start. Why?
expected_behavior: Explains that without group.id the assign container is used, and KafkaAssignConsumerContainer rejects topicsPattern in its constructor with "@KafkaListener with assign strategy (when group.id is null) does not support topicsPattern, please specify topics instead"
Explains why: a pattern subscription needs the consumer-group rebalance protocol, which assign mode does not have
Offers the two fixes: list the topics explicitly in `topics` (one or more), or add a group.id and use subscribe mode where topicsPattern works
Does not suggest that the failure is a missing single-topic limit or recommend exactly one topic

evals.query: We need to see Kafka record keys, values and headers in our Kora 2.0 consumer logs while debugging, but the JSON values contain a `password` field and the `authorization` and `x-api-key` headers must never appear in clear. How do I set this up?
expected_behavior: Enables telemetry.logging.enabled = true on the listener and sets the listener's logger (its canonical class name, under logging.levels) to TRACE, explaining that key/value/headers are added only at TRACE and only on the consumer side
Configures telemetry.logging.maskHeaders to include x-api-key, keeping authorization (the list replaces the default authorization/cookie/set-cookie; names are compared case-insensitively)
Registers a DataMasker component tagged @Tag(KafkaConsumerTelemetry.class), e.g. new JsonDataMasker(MaskingPathRules.builder().mask("password", new MaskingFull()).build())

States that no Kafka DataMasker is registered by default, so without it JSON values are logged unmasked, and that the JSON masker is chosen only when the value is read through @Json (JsonKafkaDeserializer)

Mentions that the header replacement comes from the @Tag(KafkaConsumerTelemetry.class) MaskingStrategy (default ***), and that DefaultKafkaConsumerBodyConverter can be subclassed as a @Component to change masker selection
Links or defers to the shared masking model in kora-aop-logging for MaskingPathRules / DataMasker details
Does not invent config keys such as maskBody, maskFields or logging.payload

evals.query: In Jaeger I search for spans named kafka.poll and 'orders process record' from my Kora 2.0 @KafkaListener and find nothing since the upgrade to 2.0.0.RC2. What are the span names now?
expected_behavior: Says RC2 (#972) renamed them to the OpenTelemetry messaging convention: the poll span is 'poll' and the per-record span is 'process <topic>' (here 'process orders')
Mentions messaging.operation.name = poll / process and messaging.operation.type = receive / process on those spans
Keeps the rest right: the poll span is a trace root (setNoParent) and the record span continues the producer's W3C context with a link to the poll span
Notes that messaging.process.duration and messaging.process.batch.duration now also carry messaging.operation.name = process
